physicalNotes: Radius 0.2155 Jupiter radii from Rea et al. 2026 (2026A&A...711A..86R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...711A..86R/abstract): 15,406.5 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0202 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 52.79920330011 d
sources.shape: Rea et al. 2026 (2026A&A...711A..86R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname REA_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 60.5; Rea et al. 2026 (2026A&A...711A..86R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname REA_ET_AL_2026): inclination 89.602 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2460879.886381 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 8 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
